# A bounded field guide

A map is most useful when it records both a route and the reason for taking it.[^route]

<aside data-reading-aside id="aside-observation"><strong>Field observation.</strong> A short detour can explain context without interrupting the primary route.</aside>

The second pass checks the same source again[^route] and adds a separate implementation detail.[^boundary]

An image-only note keeps its meaningful textual equivalent.[^image]

<aside data-reading-aside id="aside-boundary">The rail is deliberately finite, while the canonical article remains complete in normal document order.</aside>

The final paragraph keeps the article long enough to verify that rail entries and prose occupy distinct columns without covering one another.

[^route]: The route note remains in the canonical list and links to [an illustrative source](https://example.com/route).

[^boundary]: The boundary note verifies an independent definition and keyboard backref.
